annotations.betterLine: Cast Elspeth, Storm Slayer and use +1 to create 2 soldier tokens, building board advantage while the opponent is defenseless. The opponent lacks the resources to meaningfully answer a 6-loyalty planeswalker with token generation.

annotations.description: Casting Shock to face for 2 damage instead of deploying Hexing Squelcher. Hexing Squelcher can't be countered (safe against the UW opponent's likely countermagic), puts a 2/2 body on board for pressure, and crucially makes all spells uncounterable - enabling Nova Hellkite to land safely next turn through the opponent's No More Lies or other counters.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Shock (presumably targeting opponent's face for 2 damage)
annotations.betterLine: Cast Hexing Squelcher to apply pressure and set up an uncounterable Nova Hellkite next turn against the UW control opponent

annotations.description: Gem3P Villain declined to counter a Shock with No More Lies available. Shock deals 2 damage and at 17 life this matters, but more importantly, the opponent has very few cards and resources - countering their spells denies them tempo and card advantage. The opponent likely targeted Gem3P Villain directly (bringing them to 15) or could be targeting something relevant. With No More Lies costing only WU (which Gem3P has available via Hallowed Fountain + Island), there's little reason not to counter it. The 3 mana tax from No More Lies would almost certainly counter Shock since the opponent has 4 lands tapped (postcombat main). Additionally, letting damage through when you're already at 17 life against a red aggro deck is risky, especially when you have a 5-mana Elspeth you want to deploy next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to counter Shock with No More Lies, allowing 2 damage to resolve.
annotations.betterLine: Cast No More Lies targeting Shock to counter it. The opponent likely cannot pay {3} extra with their mana situation in postcombat main, and preserving life total against red aggro is important while setting up Elspeth next turn.

annotations.description: Activating Fountainport to create a 1/1 Fish token on their own postcombat main phase costs 3 mana + tap Fountainport + 1 life, leaving only 1 untapped land. This sacrifices the ability to hold up No More Lies (WU) against the opponent's next turn threats. A 1/1 token provides minimal value compared to keeping countermagic available when the opponent has 5 cards in hand. Additionally, they haven't played their Island from hand yet - they should play the land first if they want to maximize options.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Fountainport to create a 1/1 Fish token during their own postcombat main phase
annotations.betterLine: Play Island from hand (land drop), then pass without activating Fountainport, keeping No More Lies mana available to counter opponent's threats on their turn. If they want to use Fountainport, do it at end of opponent's turn when counter protection is less needed.

annotations.description: Gem3P Villain has 6 lands on the battlefield with nothing else to spend mana on during the postcombat main phase. Fountainport can create a Treasure token for {4},{T}, which would effectively bank mana for future turns and help cast Elspeth (5 mana) next turn even through potential land issues. Additionally, with Elspeth's token-doubling ability in hand, creating tokens from Fountainport has extra synergy. Passing with 6 untapped mana and no instant-speed interaction worth holding up (No More Lies costs only 2) wastes potential value from the mana sink.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating Fountainport or Restless Anchorage, leaving mana unused.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Fountainport to create a Treasure token ({4},{T}), banking mana for next turn's Elspeth cast while still having mana available for No More Lies if needed on opponent's turn.

annotations.description: With no opposing creatures on board and the opponent having only 4 mana available (limited to burn spells as interaction), this was likely the best window to deploy Elspeth, Storm Slayer. On an empty board, Elspeth immediately +1s to 6 loyalty with a 1/1 soldier (doubled to two 1/1s), and the opponent's burn (at most Lightning Strike for 3 + Shock for 2 = 5 damage to planeswalker) likely can't kill her in one turn, especially through blockers. Passing to hold up No More Lies is defensible but overly conservative when the opponent's threat density is limited by their 4 available mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed the turn to hold up No More Lies (WU) countermagic
annotations.betterLine: Cast Elspeth, Storm Slayer and +1 to create soldier tokens on an empty board, establishing a win condition while the opponent lacks board presence to pressure it effectively

annotations.description: Gem3P Villain passed their entire turn without casting Elspeth, Storm Slayer on a completely empty opposing board. With 5 available mana (Plains, Hallowed Fountain for WW, plus Island, Fountainport, Restless Anchorage for generic), Elspeth could be deployed immediately, going to 6 loyalty with +1 and creating 2 soldier tokens (due to the doubling static). The opponent has no creatures and only 4 lands, making this an ideal window. Additionally, Restless Anchorage could have been animated to attack as a 2/3 flyer.
annotations.actionTaken: Skipped precombat main phase entirely, doing nothing with 5 available mana, then skipped attack.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Elspeth, Storm Slayer, use +1 to create 2 soldier tokens on an empty board. This starts generating massive value with no opposing threats to contest it.

annotations.description: Gem3P Villain declined to activate Restless Anchorage during combat. The opponent has no untapped mana (only one tapped Mountain and three untapped Mountains plus Rockface Village), but their burn spells cost 1R (Shock) or 1R (Lightning Strike) — both already in the graveyard. With no cards in the opponent's hand that we know threaten the land, and the opponent's board being empty of creatures, attacking for 2 flying damage and creating a Map token (which can later be sacrificed for value via Fountainport's draw ability) is essentially free. The risk of losing Restless Anchorage to removal is minimal since the opponent's known burn is in the graveyard, and 2 damage chips away at the opponent's life total while generating incremental value.

annotations.betterLine: Activate Restless Anchorage for {1}{W}{U}, attack for 2 flying damage, create a Map token (which can later be sacrificed to Fountainport to draw a card). The opponent has no known instant-speed removal available to punish this.

annotations.description: With all opponent lands tapped (no countermagic threat), casting Nova Hellkite (4/5 flying haste) would be stronger. It can immediately attack Elspeth for 4 damage (5→1) while leaving a major threat on board, compared to Lightning Strike which deals only 3 damage and leaves less board presence. The opponent being fully tapped out makes this the ideal window to resolve the most impactful threat.

annotations.betterLine: Cast Nova Hellkite with 5 Mountains, attack Elspeth Storm Slayer with the 4/5 flying haste creature, bringing Elspeth to 1 loyalty while establishing a dominant board presence with opponent tapped out

annotations.actionTaken: Cast Hexing Squelcher (a 2/2 with no relevant abilities this turn) instead of playing Mountain and casting Nova Hellkite.
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain from hand, then cast Nova Hellkite (3RR) with the 5 remaining mana after Lightning Strike resolves. Nova Hellkite's flying haste body would deal significantly more damage and apply much greater pressure.

annotations.description: MiniMx Libby played a Mountain before casting Nova Hellkite. They already have 5 mountains (4 Mountain + 1 Rockface Village) which is exactly enough to cast Nova Hellkite (3RR) using Warp (2R) or normal cost. Playing the land first is fine for mana, but the real issue is that they chose to play Mountain instead of casting Nova Hellkite. With Elspeth at 5 loyalty on the opponent's board (which creates tokens doubled and can destroy creatures), getting a hasty 4/5 flyer on board immediately is critical. Nova Hellkite with haste can attack Elspeth for 4 damage (bringing her to 1 loyalty) or hit the opponent's face. The opponent has 13 life and MiniMx has 2 Nova Hellkites and a Lightning Strike in hand (3+4+4 = 11 damage potential over upcoming turns). Every turn Elspeth stays alive, the opponent gains more advantage through doubled tokens and +1/+1 counters. Playing Mountain and passing without casting Nova Hellkite would waste a critical turn. However, looking more carefully - this is just the land drop decision, and they may still cast Nova Hellkite after playing the land. Playing the land first before casting spells is actually correct sequencing. But wait - they already had 5 lands (4 Mountains + 1 Rockface Village), which gives them exactly 5 mana for Nova Hellkite's {3}{R}{R} cost. The 6th land doesn't help cast anything additional this turn. The sequencing of land before spell is fine and standard practice. Actually, this is just playing a land - they can still cast Nova Hellkite this turn. This isn't a blunder at all since playing land before spells is correct sequencing.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mountain from hand
annotations.betterLine: This is actually correct sequencing - play land first, then cast spells. No blunder.

annotations.description: Casting Nova Hellkite at full cost into Elspeth, Storm Slayer at 5 loyalty. Elspeth can simply use her -3 to destroy Nova Hellkite (MV 5 >= 3) next turn, effectively trading a premium threat for a planeswalker activation that still leaves Elspeth alive at 2 loyalty. Meanwhile, a Warp Hellkite + Lightning Strike line would kill Elspeth entirely.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Nova Hellkite at full cost (5 mana), leaving Elspeth alive at 5 loyalty and vulnerable to her -3 removal.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Nova Hellkite for Warp cost ({2}{R} = 3 mana) + Lightning Strike targeting Elspeth (2 mana, 5→2 loyalty), then attack Elspeth with the 4/5 flying haste Hellkite to kill her. Eliminates the biggest threat on board, and the Hellkite can be recast from exile later.

annotations.description: Nova Hellkite (a 4/5 flying haste creature) is on the stack and Gem3P Villain has No More Lies in hand with the mana to cast it (Hallowed Fountain + Plains are untapped, providing W and U). At 13 life facing an aggressive red deck that has already burned them with Lightning Strikes and Shocks, letting a 4/5 flying haste creature resolve is devastating. Nova Hellkite will deal 1 damage to a creature on ETB and then attack for 4 in the air immediately, putting Gem3P Villain to 9 life or lower. With the opponent having cards in hand that are likely more burn spells, this could easily be lethal. Elspeth's soldier tokens can't block a flyer effectively. This is a must-counter threat.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, allowing Nova Hellkite to resolve uncountered.
annotations.betterLine: Cast No More Lies targeting Nova Hellkite on the stack. The opponent likely cannot pay the additional {3} given their mana situation, and even if they can, it's worth attempting to counter the most threatening card they've played. Day of Judgment in hand is a backup plan but costs a full turn and doesn't prevent the haste damage.

annotations.description: Opponent has only 1 untapped Mountain, making it extremely unlikely they cast anything meaningful. Gem3P Villain could have used Fountainport to create a Fish token (doubled to 2 by Elspeth's static ability) for future chump blocking or card draw via Fountainport's sacrifice ability, instead of holding up mana for No More Lies against an opponent who can't cast anything significant.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating any abilities, keeping mana open unnecessarily.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Fountainport ({3}, {T}, Pay 1 life) to create a Fish token, which Elspeth doubles to 2 tokens. These provide future blockers for Nova Hellkite and fuel for Fountainport's card draw ability.

annotations.description: Gem3P Villain is at 9 life facing a Nova Hellkite (4/5 flying haste) that will untap next turn. The opponent has 6 lands (one untapped Mountain) and has already cast Lightning Strike x2 and Shock from the graveyard, meaning burn spells are a real threat. Day of Judgment would destroy the Nova Hellkite and any other creatures cleanly, while Elspeth survives as a planeswalker. Instead, they used Elspeth's +1 to create a soldier token, which doesn't address the 4-damage flying threat that will attack next turn. The soldier tokens will also die to Day of Judgment if cast later, wasting the token creation. At 9 life, taking 4 from Hellkite puts them to 5, well within burn range (Lightning Strike = 3, Shock = 2). They should cast Day of Judgment immediately to remove the Hellkite, then use Elspeth's +1 to start rebuilding.
annotations.actionTaken: Used Elspeth's +1 to create a soldier token before dealing with Nova Hellkite
annotations.betterLine: Cast Day of Judgment immediately to destroy Nova Hellkite (the only creature threatening lethal damage), then use Elspeth's +1 to create tokens and rebuild the board safely

Playing the land first is fine but not casting Get Lost afterward wastes the opportunity to remove the immediate lethal threat.

annotations.betterLine: Play Island, then cast Get Lost targeting Nova Hellkite to remove the 4/5 flying threat while preserving the Soldier token board. At 9 life facing a dragon and an opponent with burn spells in graveyard, removing the threat immediately is critical.
